translation_en: Sadaqah ibn al-Fadl narrated to us; Ibn Uyaynah informed us, saying: I heard al-Zuhri, from Ubaydullah, from Umm Qays bint Mihsan, who said: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “Use this Indian wood, for it contains seven remedies. It is used as nasal medicine for tonsillitis and administered into the side of the mouth for pleurisy.” She also came to the Prophet with a young son of hers who had not yet begun eating solid food. He urinated on him, so the Prophet called for water and sprinkled it over him.

Abu Mamar narrated to us; Abd al-Warith narrated to us; Ayyub narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, had cupping performed while fasting.
Musaddad narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr, from Tawus and Ata, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, had cupping performed while in ihram.

Muhammad ibn Muqatil narrated to us; Abdullah informed us; Humayd al-Tawil informed us, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who was asked about the cupper's payment. He said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, had cupping performed; Abu Taybah did it for him, and he gave him two measures of food. He spoke to his masters, who reduced what he owed them. He said: “The best remedies you use are cupping and Indian costus.” He also said: “Do not treat your children by pressing their uvulas; use costus.”

Said ibn Talid narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to me, saying: Amr and another person informed me that Bukayr narrated to him that Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah narrated to him that Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with them both, visited al-Muqanna. He then said: “I will not leave until you have cupping performed, for I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: ‘There is healing in it.’”

Ismail narrated to us: Sulayman narrated to me, from Alqamah, who heard Abd al-Rahman al-Araj, who heard Abdullah ibn Buhaynah relate that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, had cupping performed at Lahy Jamal, on the road to Mecca, while in ihram, on the middle of his head. Al-Ansari said: Hisham ibn Hassan informed us; Ikrimah narrated to us, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah had cupping performed on his head.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me; Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Hisham, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, had cupping performed on his head while in ihram, because of an ailment he had, at a place called Lahy Jamal. Muhammad ibn Sawa said: Hisham informed us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of Allah had cupping performed on his head while in ihram because of a migraine he had.

Ismail ibn Aban narrated to us; Ibn al-Ghasil narrated to us, saying: Asim ibn Umar narrated to me, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “If there is healing in any of your remedies, it is in a drink of honey, the incision of cupping, or a cauterizing touch with fire. I do not like to be cauterized.”

Musaddad narrated to us; Hammad narrated to us, from Ayyub, who said: I heard Mujahid, from Ibn Abi Layla, from Kab—Ibn Ujrah—who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, came to me at the time of al-Hudaybiyah while I was tending a fire beneath a cooking pot and lice were falling from my head. He said: “Are the lice bothering you?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “Shave your head and fast for three days, or feed six needy people, or offer a sacrifice.” Ayyub said: I do not know which of these he mentioned first.

Abu al-Walid Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik narrated to us; Abd al-Rahman ibn Sulayman ibn al-Ghasil narrated to us; Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah narrated to us, saying: I heard Jabir narrate from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “If any of your remedies brings healing, it is in the incision of cupping or a cauterizing touch with fire. I do not like to be cauterized.”

Imran ibn Maysarah narrated to us; Ibn Fudayl narrated to us; Husayn narrated to us, from Amir, from Imran ibn Husayn, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: “No incantation is [especially warranted] except for the evil eye or a venomous sting.” I mentioned this to Said ibn Jubayr, and he said: Ibn Abbas narrated to us that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The nations were shown to me. A prophet and two prophets passed by with small groups, and a prophet passed by with no one. Then a great multitude was raised up before me. I said: ‘Is this my community?’ It was said: ‘This is Moses and his people.’ Then I was told: ‘Look toward the horizon.’ There was a multitude filling it. I was told: ‘Look here and there at the horizons of the sky.’ There was a multitude filling them. It was said: ‘This is your community, and seventy thousand of them will enter Paradise without reckoning.’” Then he went inside without explaining further. The people discussed it, saying: “We believed in Allah and followed His Messenger, so perhaps we are they—or our children born in Islam. We were born in the pre-Islamic age.” The Prophet heard of this, came out, and said: “They are those who do not ask others to perform incantations for them, do not regard omens as bad, do not seek cauterization, and put their trust in their Lord.” Ukkashah ibn Mihsan said: “Am I one of them, Messenger of Allah?” He said: “Yes.” Another man stood and asked the same. He said: “Ukkashah has preceded you.”

Musaddad narrated to us; Yahya narrated to us, from Shu'bah, who said: Humayd ibn Nafi narrated to me, from Zaynab, from Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her: A woman's husband died, and her eye became sore. They mentioned her condition and the use of kohl to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said they feared for her eye. He said: “One of you used to remain in her house in the worst of her worn furnishings—or in her worn furnishings in the worst of her house—and when a dog passed, she would throw a piece of dung. No: [the waiting period is] four months and ten days.”

Affan said: Sulaym ibn Hayyan narrated to us; Said ibn Mina narrated to us, who said: I heard Abu Hurairah say: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “There is no contagion [that operates independently], no belief in the ominous month of Safar, no bird-omen, and no Hamah omen. Flee from a leper as you would flee from a lion.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us; Ghundar narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik, who said: I heard Amr ibn Hurayth say: I heard Said ibn Zayd say: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “Truffles are a kind of manna, and their juice is a cure for the eye.” Shu'bah said: Al-Hakam ibn Utaybah informed me, from al-Hasan al-Urani, from Amr ibn Hurayth, from Said ibn Zayd, from the Prophet, the same report. Shu'bah said: When al-Hakam narrated it to me, I did not doubt that it was the report of Abd al-Malik.

Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Yahya ibn Said narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Abi Aishah narrated to me, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah, from Ibn Abbas and Aishah, that Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, kissed the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, after he had died. Aishah said: We administered medicine into his mouth during his illness, and he gestured to us not to do so. We said: “A sick person dislikes medicine.” When he recovered, he said: “Did I not forbid you to administer medicine into my mouth?” We said: “A sick person dislikes medicine.” He said: “Let no one in the house remain without having medicine administered into his mouth while I watch, except al-Abbas, for he was not present with you.”

Ali ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Ubaydullah informed me, from Umm Qays, who said: I brought a son of mine to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, after I had treated his tonsillitis by pressing his uvula. He said: “Why do you press your children's uvulas with this treatment? Use Indian wood, for it contains seven remedies, including pleurisy. It is used as nasal medicine for tonsillitis and administered into the side of the mouth for pleurisy.” I heard al-Zuhri say: He explained two of them to us and did not explain five. I said to Sufyan: “Mamar says, ‘I treated him.’” He replied: “He did not preserve the wording ‘I treated him’ from him; I preserved it directly from al-Zuhri.” Sufyan described the boy as having his palate lifted with a finger; Sufyan put his finger into the boy's mouth and explained that it meant lifting his palate with his finger. He did not say to administer anything into his mouth.

Bishr ibn Muhammad informed us; Abdullah informed us; Mamar and Yunus informed us. Al-Zuhri said: Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah informed me that Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, the wife of the Prophet, said: When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, became very ill, he asked his wives for permission to be cared for in my house. They permitted him. He came out supported by two men, his feet dragging on the ground, between al-Abbas and another man. I told Ibn Abbas, who asked: “Do you know who the other man was, whom Aishah did not name?” I said: “No.” He said: “It was Ali.” Aishah said: After the Prophet entered her house and his illness became severe, he said: “Pour water over me from seven waterskins whose ties have not been undone, so that I may address the people.” They seated him in a basin belonging to Hafsah, the Prophet's wife, and began pouring water from those waterskins over him until he gestured that they had done enough. She said: He went out to the people, led them in prayer, and addressed them.

Abu al-Yaman narrated to us; Shuayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah informed me that Umm Qays bint Mihsan al-Asadiyyah—of Asad of Khuzaymah, one of the first emigrant women to pledge allegiance to the Prophet, and the sister of Ukkashah—informed him that she brought a son of hers to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, after treating him for tonsillitis by pressing his uvula. The Prophet said: “Why do you press your children’s uvulas with this treatment? Use Indian wood, for it contains seven remedies, including pleurisy.” He meant costus, which is Indian wood. Yunus and Ishaq ibn Rashid reported from al-Zuhri the wording: “She treated him.”

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Jafar narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Mutawakkil, from Abu Said, who said: A man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: “My brother has severe diarrhea.” He said: “Give him honey to drink.” The man gave it to him, then said: “I gave it to him, but it only made his diarrhea worse.” He said: “Allah has spoken the truth, but your brother's stomach has lied.” Al-Nadr also reported it from Shu'bah.

Abd al-Aziz ibn Abdullah narrated to us; Ibrahim ibn Sad narrated to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman and another person informed me that Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “There is no contagion [that operates independently], no belief in the ominous month of Safar, and no bird-omen.” A Bedouin said: “Messenger of Allah, what about my camels? They are like gazelles in the sand, then a mangy camel comes among them and makes them mange.” He said: “Then who infected the first one?” Al-Zuhri reported it from Abu Salamah and Sinan ibn Abi Sinan.

Muhammad narrated to me; Attab ibn Bashir informed us, from Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, who said: Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah informed me that Umm Qays bint Mihsan, one of the first women to emigrate and pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah, and sister of Ukkashah ibn Mihsan, informed him that she brought a son of hers to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, after treating him for tonsillitis by pressing his uvula. He said: “Fear Allah! Why do you press your children's uvulas with these treatments? Use Indian wood, for it contains seven remedies, including pleurisy.” He meant costus, meaning al-qust; this is a dialectal form.

Arim narrated to us; Hammad narrated to us, saying: Some of the books of Abu Qilabah were read to Ayyub; some reports in them he had narrated and some were read to him. This was written in the book from Anas: Abu Talhah and Anas ibn al-Nadr cauterized him, and Abu Talhah cauterized him with his own hand. Abbad ibn Mansur reported from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, permitted a household from the Ansar to use incantations for a venomous sting and an ear ailment. Anas said: I was cauterized for pleurisy while the Messenger of Allah was alive. Abu Talhah, Anas ibn al-Nadr, and Zayd ibn Thabit witnessed it, and Abu Talhah cauterized me.

Said ibn Ufair narrated to me; Yaqoub ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Qari narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sad al-Saidi, who said: When the helmet was broken on the head of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, his face was bloodied, and one of his front teeth was broken, Ali kept bringing water in a shield. Fatimah came and washed the blood from his face. When Fatimah, peace be upon her, saw that the blood exceeded the water, she took a mat, burned it, and placed it on the wound of the Messenger of Allah. The bleeding stopped.

Yahya ibn Sulayman narrated to me; Ibn Wahb narrated to me, saying: Malik narrated to me, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “Fever is from the breath of Hell, so cool it with water.” Nafi said: Abdullah used to say: “Remove the affliction from us.”

Abdullah ibn Maslamah narrated to us, from Malik, from Hisham, from Fatimah bint al-Mundhir, that Asma bint Abi Bakr, may Allah be pleased with them both, when a woman with fever was brought to her, would pray for her and take water and pour it between her and the opening of her garment. She said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to instruct us to cool fever with water.

Said ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us; Ismail ibn Ibrahim ibn Uqbah narrated to us, saying: Nafi informed me, from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “While three men were walking, rain caught them, so they took shelter in a cave in a mountain. A rock slid down from the mountain and blocked the cave entrance. They said to one another: ‘Consider righteous deeds you did for Allah, and call upon Allah by them; perhaps He will remove this rock.’ One of them said: ‘O Allah, I had two elderly parents and young children whom I supported. When I returned in the evening and milked the animals, I would give my parents to drink before my children. One day I went far in search of trees and did not return until evening. I found them asleep. I milked as usual and stood by their heads with the milk, unwilling to wake them and unwilling to give my children theirs first. My children were crying at my feet. That remained my practice and theirs until dawn. If You know I did that seeking Your pleasure, open an opening for us through which we may see the sky.’ Allah opened an opening for them through which they could see the sky. The second man said: ‘O Allah, I had a female cousin whom I loved more than men love women. I sought intimacy with her, but she refused until I gave her one hundred dinars. I worked until I gathered one hundred dinars and brought them to her. When I sat between her legs, she said: “Servant of Allah, fear Allah and do not break the seal [of chastity].” So I left her. O Allah, if You know I did that seeking Your pleasure, open another part for us.’ Allah opened another part for them. The third man said: ‘O Allah, I hired a worker for a measure of rice. When he finished his work, he said: “Give me my due.” I offered him his wage, but he left it and turned away from it. I kept investing it until it grew into cattle and their herder. He later came and said: “Fear Allah and do not wrong me; give me my due.” I said: “Go to those cattle and their herder.” He said: “Fear Allah and do not mock me.” I said: “I am not mocking you; take those cattle and their herder.” He took them and went away. If You know I did that seeking Your pleasure, remove what remains of the obstruction.’ Then Allah removed it all for them.”

Sad ibn Hafs narrated to us; Shayban narrated to us, from Mansur, from al-Musayyab, from Warad, from al-Mughirah, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “Allah has forbidden you to disobey mothers, to withhold what is due while demanding what is yours, and to bury daughters alive. He dislikes for you idle talk, excessive questioning, and wasting wealth.”

Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to us, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, that Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mutim said: Jubayr ibn Mutim informed him that he heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “One who severs family ties will not enter Paradise.”

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to me; Muhammad ibn Main narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Said ibn Abi Said, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “Whoever wishes to have his provision expanded and his life prolonged, let him maintain ties of kinship.”

Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us; al-Layth narrated to us, from Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Anas ibn Malik informed me that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Whoever wishes to have his provision expanded and his life prolonged, let him maintain ties of kinship.”
